title: the products query, one clause at a time

steps.sql:
SELECT category, count(*) AS n, round(avg(price), 2) AS avg_price
FROM products
WHERE NOT discontinued
GROUP BY category
HAVING count(*) >= 10
ORDER BY avg_price DESC
LIMIT 3

stages.note: FROM hands over all 200 products. a table has no order of its own, so they're drawn with the 12 discontinued ones on top, where you can watch them go.
stages.sql: SELECT id, category, price, discontinued, name FROM products ORDER BY discontinued DESC, id
SELECT id, category, price, discontinued, name FROM products WHERE NOT discontinued ORDER BY id

stages.note: the same 188 rows, sorted into 11 buckets, one per category. the 3 products with no category share a bucket: when grouping, NULLs count as equal.
stages.sql: SELECT id, category, price, discontinued, name FROM products WHERE NOT discontinued ORDER BY category NULLS FIRST, id

stages.note: HAVING judges whole buckets, never single rows. the NULL bucket's count(*) is 3, so it goes, all 3 rows at once. 10 buckets are left.
stages.sql:
SELECT id, category, price, discontinued, name
FROM (SELECT p.*, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS rows_in_bucket FROM products AS p WHERE NOT discontinued) AS b
WHERE rows_in_bucket >= 10
ORDER BY category NULLS FIRST, id
SELECT category, count(*) AS n, round(avg(price), 2) AS avg_price FROM products WHERE NOT discontinued GROUP BY category HAVING count(*) >= 10 ORDER BY category
SELECT category, count(*) AS n, round(avg(price), 2) AS avg_price FROM products WHERE NOT discontinued GROUP BY category HAVING count(*) >= 10 ORDER BY avg_price DESC
